body.x: A conventional circuit board is built to sit flat. A patch on the skin, a band around the neck or the joint of a robot is not flat, and it bends, stretches and moves with whatever it is attached to.
What if the circuit itself could do the same?

That is the premise of T&L Healthcare, a company in Suji-gu, Yongin, Gyeonggi Province, that develops next-generation flexible circuits and devices. Led by CEO Dogi Pyeon, the company will take part in KES 2026, where it plans to focus on technology and module sales built on its proprietary patented SPCB (Stretchable PCB) technology.

T&L Healthcare, which was founded in 2023, says SPCB overcomes the limitations of conventional printed circuit boards (PCBs) and flexible PCBs (FPCBs) by providing high flexibility and stretchability. According to the company, that lets devices conform to body curves and movement, and makes the technology applicable to wearable devices and patches that fit the human body as well as to robotics and other fields that need flexible, dynamic structures. It says SPCB can be combined with LEDs, sensors and other functions, and that it develops customized modules and devices to widen the range of industries where the technology is used.

At the exhibition, the company will show products built on SPCB: COMLAX, NECKCARE BAND GOLDEN and the LED Cool Face Mask. T&L Healthcare says the combination of flexibility and stretchability is what sets SPCB apart, and that it allows customized development for each product as well as collaboration on an original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and original design manufacturer (ODM) basis.

On its record, the company says that since 2025 it has been expanding strategic partnerships and signing memoranda of understanding (MOUs) with major Korean corporations and with healthcare and beauty companies, all based on SPCB. It reports that it is carrying out joint R&D projects with a range of partners that want to apply the technology to new products, including wearable devices, patches and LED-based solutions, and that it is working to commercialize the technology in these fields. T&L Healthcare also says it is widening business-to-business (B2B) cooperation at home and abroad through the supply of SPCB technology and modules and through customized product development.

T&L Healthcare currently has no exports. Rather than focusing on particular countries, the company says it aims to enter global markets where demand for SPCB technology is strong. It is looking in particular for partners that develop or manufacture wearable devices, patches, healthcare and beauty devices, robotics and other products that need flexibility and stretchability, and it says it will pursue technology application, joint R&D, SPCB module supply and OEM/ODM partnerships with them.

Its plan is to find overseas companies that are seeking flexible and stretchable circuit technology, to pursue technology application and joint R&D with them, and to expand its B2B business through supplying SPCB modules and technology. The company also intends to develop and commercialize wearable devices, patches and healthcare and beauty devices with global partners, widening its overseas presence step by step.

Its main difficulty is finding those partners. T&L Healthcare says a lack of information about overseas markets and about companies that need the technology makes it hard to identify potential partners, and that support in locating overseas buyers and technology-seeking companies, along with local market information, would help speed its entry into global markets.

The company's stated goals for KES 2026 are to introduce what SPCB can do and where it can be applied to Korean and international companies, to find new partners for technology application and joint R&D, and to widen opportunities for technology sales, commercialization and B2B collaboration.

KES 2026 is the 57th edition of Korea Electronics Show, organized by the Korea Electronics Association (KEA) and hosted by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources. It runs from Tuesday, Oct. 13, to Friday, Oct. 16, at COEX in Seoul under the theme "AI in Motion." The show covers seven sectors: electronic parts and materials, AI transformation (AX), mobility solutions, robotics, digital health innovations, ESG sustainability, and Web3.0 and XR. Organizers expect about 500 exhibitors and 70,000 visitors.
